member.name: T:Gtk.Windows.FormsDesigner.configProperties
member.summary: Represents configuration properties that control runtime serialization and application path settings.
member.remarks: This class provides options for enabling unsafe binary formatter serialization and for setting application paths via host policy. These properties correspond to runtime configuration switches and may affect application security and startup behavior. Use caution when enabling unsafe serialization features, as they may introduce security risks.

member.name: P:Gtk.Windows.FormsDesigner.configProperties.EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether support for unsafe BinaryFormatter serialization is enabled.
member.remarks: Enabling unsafe BinaryFormatter serialization allows deserialization of types using BinaryFormatter, which can introduce security vulnerabilities. It is recommended to disable this setting unless compatibility with legacy data is required. Use with caution in production environments.

member.name: T:Gtk.Windows.FormsDesigner.DesignerConfig
member.summary: Writes the two files Visual Studio launches the out-of-process Windows Forms designer server with.

remarks.para: A GTK project targets a plain netX.0 moniker with UseWindowsForms off, so the SDK writes it a designer runtimeconfig naming Microsoft.NETCore.App alone. The designer server is a real Windows Forms process: started that way it cannot load System.Windows.Forms and dies, and the IDE reports a ServerProcess failure instead of opening the form. Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App has to be there as well.

The dependency list stays empty for the opposite reason: with the project's package closure in it the server resolves System.Windows.Forms from the GTK implementation the project compiles against rather than from the shared framework. What the designer needs beyond the framework comes from the shadow-copied output directory, through SetAppPaths.
Kept free of Microsoft.Build so the rules can be tested without an MSBuild host; is only the task wrapper.
